page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 4 dedicated physical cores utilizing the AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include any local storage or GPU accelerators, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate that the ecs.g6a.xlarge occupies a lower-tier performance profile. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests place the instance in the bottom 10% of tested hardware, with scores of 762.69 and 1531.17 respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show weak performance, with read-only large block speeds at 31.83 GB/sec and write speeds at 16.28 GB/sec. However, the instance achieves average performance in specific workloads, such as single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 9.2 GB/sec, Geekbench single-core scoring at 1282.0, and PassMark CPU encryption testing at 4224.57.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.g6a.xlarge is its modest computational and memory throughput relative to its dedicated core allocation. While the dedicated AMD EPYC cores prevent resource contention from noisy neighbors, the overall processing capacity remains limited, as evidenced by a PassMark database operations score of 1379.06 and a Redis SET throughput of 3.6 million operations per second. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance serves as an entry-level option for workloads requiring dedicated x86_64 resources without the premium cost of high-frequency or memory-optimized hardware.

Given its balanced resource ratio but lower-tier benchmark performance, the ecs.g6a.xlarge is suited for lightweight general-purpose applications. Appropriate workloads include basic web serving, development and testing environments, code compilation tasks of moderate size, and low-throughput background utility services. It is not recommended for high-performance database hosting, real-time data processing, or memory-intensive applications.
